conclusion_finding: The proposition itself HOLDS. I ran an exhaustive check of every integer n in [1, 337343] in exact Python integer arithmetic (no floating point anywhere). The maximum stopping time on the whole stated domain is 442, attained at n = 230631, and 442 < 443. Zero n in the domain have T(n) >= 443. Because the stated domain is finite and my search covered it completely, the bound 337343 coincides with the domain, so the check is exhaustive rather than merely bounded; I report it as bounded_search rather than proof to avoid overstating a machine sweep as a mathematical proof.
broken_step_explanation: Step s8 reads: 'The sweep covers [1, 4052]; the statement is asserted for every n in [1, 337343].' This is a bare assertion, not an inference. s2 establishes the property only on [1, 4052]; s8 extends it to a domain 83x larger, leaving 333,291 integers (4053..337343) entirely uncovered by any step of the argument. No step supplies an induction, a monotonicity property, a residue-class reduction, or any other device that would let a verified initial segment imply the tail -- and for Collatz stopping time no such device is available, since stopping time is not monotone in n. The gap is not merely formal: the true maximum of the argument's target quantity occurs at n = 230631, which lies OUTSIDE the swept range [1, 4052] (whose own maximum is only 237). So the extremal case that actually decides the proposition is exactly the case the argument never examines. The argument would read identically if the true record were 500, in which case its conclusion would be false; an argument whose conclusion is independent of its evidence does not establish that conclusion.
secondary_defect: Steps s3 through s7 are all individually TRUE (I verified each over the exact range it states: n^3 = n mod 6 on [1,2000]; 5^3-5 = 120; n^2 >= 2n on [2,2000]; (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) on [1,2000] with H(n)=n^2+[n=3], which holds trivially since the indicator only fires at n=3 where the factor (n-3) vanishes; 4|n => n(n+1)/2 even on [1,2000]). But none of them mentions the Collatz map, stopping time, or the number 443, and none is used by s8 for anything. They are true but inert filler whose declared 'depends_on' edges manufacture the appearance of a derivation chain. Their truth is therefore not a defense of the argument; the argument is invalid on s8 regardless.
